13. Dr Shadeen Malik further submits that to deal with the energy resources of the Republic is essentially a function of the Government of Bangladesh and the BERC being empowered by the Parliament to deal with some of the aspects and functions in relation to the energy resources of Bangladesh is performing functions which clearly and obviously 'in respect of the Government of Bangladesh' as gas (a mineral) is vested in the Government as provided by Article 143 of the Constitution and therefore the office of the Chairman of the BERC is, no doubt, an office in the service of Republic. 

 14. Dr Shadeen Malik next submits that the functions which are now being performed by the BERC under the Act No. 13 of 2003 were performed directly by the Government through the relevant Ministry; but the Parliament in its wisdom thought it expedient and desirable to in trust those functions to an independent body to ensure accountability and public/private involvement in regulating the energy sector and mere establishment of the BERC to that effect does not mean that the Government has completely divested itself of its sovereign and executive rights and power over mineral resources such as gas in that the BERC can not dilute the power and authority of the Republic under Article 143 of the Constitution. 

 82. We are in full agreement with the submission of Dr Shadeen Malik that to deal with the energy resources of the Republic is essentially a function of the Government and the BERC being empowered by the Parliament to deal with some of the aspects and functions vis-a-vis the energy resources or Bangladesh is performing functions which are 'in respect of the Government of Bangladesh' as gas (a mineral) is vested in the Government as provided Article 143 of the Constitution. 

 83. We find substance in the content ion of Dr Shadeen Malik that the functions which are now being performed by the BERC under the Act No. 13 of 2003 previously performed directly by the Government, but the Parliament in its wisdom thought it expedient and desirable to entrust those functions to the BERC to ensure accordingly and publie/private involvement in regulating the energy sector and mere establishment of the BERC does not mean that the Government has completely itself or its sovereign and executive rights and power mineral resources in that the BERC cannot dilute the power and authority of the Republic under Article 143 of the Constitution.
